_comment: Synthetic fourteen-masternode chain for ops/tests/test_dsl_enforcement_replay.py.
Fourteen and not fewer: with six members one missed masternode is already 16.7% of the
list and the 15% mass-outage guard swallows every epoch -- the first draft of this fixture
did exactly that and no counter ever moved. With fourteen, one miss is 7.1%, two are 14.3%
(below the guard), three are 21.4% (the guard opens).
The proTxHashes are chosen so that display order (01.., 02.., ..., 0e..) is the REVERSE of
the node's internal byte order (last byte 22 < 33 < ... < ff): canonical index 0 is member
N (0e..22) and index 13 is member A (01..ff). A tool that sorts display strings puts A at 0.
Members by canonical index: 13=A 12=B 11=C ... 0=N.
Story: A (index 13) misses epochs 2-6 -> counter 1..5, suspended at epoch 5 (count 4),
banned at epoch 6 (count 5, height 168). B (index 12) misses epoch 3 (counter 1), is
UNOBSERVED in epoch 4 while that streak is live (the hold branch no recorded devnet epoch
has exercised), is online in epoch 5 (reset). Epoch 2 is format v1 (everyone observed).
Epoch 7 is absent (freeze). Epoch 8 is a mass outage (3 of 14 = 21.4%): nothing changes.
Epoch 9: A online -> recovered; B missed -> counter 1. Epoch 10 has a wrong listSize and
must be skipped, so C (index 11) is never counted.
Epoch 11: N (index 0) is missed, but N left the list during the epoch -- the test builds
the base list of epoch 12 (the list at boundary 288) without N -- so the node skips it
(deterministicmns.cpp:423) and the counter must not move. Without that list the tool
counts N and says it could not tell.
Epoch 3's stored missedProTxHashes is DELIBERATELY the display-order resolution (indices
13 and 12 read in display order are N and M), so the cross-check warning must fire there
and nowhere else.
